headline: Approved a 2026-2029 Collective Bargaining Agreement, closures on Southern Spring Street and Thomas Drive, and six funding and purchase orders.
summary: Mayor David Morse announced Bruno Inacio as the new Finance Director. The council amended the Code of Ordinances for seven boards and committees and voted 4-2-1 to change how residents disclose their address during public comment. Councilors also passed the first reading of an order to buy portable traffic signals for Public Services.
decisions: Approved Orders 2026-96 through 2026-101 on funds, police equipment, a pump station roof, and a compactor, by a 5-0-2 vote.
Approved the 2026-2029 Collective Bargaining Agreement with the Westbrook General Unit, by a 5-0-2 vote.
Approved street closures on Southern Spring Street and Thomas Drive for utility installation, by a 5-0-2 vote.
Approved amending the Code of Ordinances for seven city boards and committees, by a 5-0-2 vote.
Approved amending the council rules on disclosure of address during public comment, by a 4-2-1 vote.
Approved the first of two readings of an order to buy portable traffic signals for Public Services, by a show of hands with none opposed.

plain_text:
WESTBROOK CITY COUNCIL 
SPECIAL CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES 
MONDAY, SEPTEMBER 21, 2026 AT 6:00 PM  
WESTBROOK HIGH SCHOOL (ROOM 114) 
125 STROUDWATER ST.  
 
 
 
  
I. READING THE CALL FOR A SPECIAL CITY COUNCIL MEETING  
 
City Clerk Ellis Ledoux noted for the record that a Special City Council meeting was called by Mayor David Morse 
on September 18,2026. Notice of the meeting was emailed to City Councilors and posted to the City's website. 
 
  
II. LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT STATEMENT 
Meeting called to order at 6:00pm by City Council President Jennifer Munro. City Clerk Ellis Ledoux read the City 
Council Land Acknowledgment statement into the record. 
 
  
III. ROLL CALL 
City Councilors Present: Michael Shaughnessy (At-Large, Vice-President)(arrived at 6:32pm), Brian McCambridge 
(Ward 1),Victor Chau (Ward 2), Amy Faulkingham (Ward 4), Jennifer Munro (Ward 5, President), Gary Rairdon 
(At-Large) 
 
City Councilors Absent: Anna A. Turcotte (Ward 3) 
 
Other City Officials Present: Eric Dudley (Director of Engineering & Public Services), Jennie Franceschi (Assistant 
City Administrator), Cameron Ferrante (Legal Counsel), Greg Hamilton (Director of Emergency Communications 
& IT), Angela Holmes (City Administrator), Sean Lally (Police Chief), Ellis Ledoux (City Clerk), Joanne LePauloue 
(Director of Human Resources), David Morse (Mayor), Robyn Saunders (Project Manager), Stephen Sloan (Fire 
Chief), Monique Cornett (Director of Economic Development), Rebecca Spitella (Director of Planning & Code 
Enforcement), Douglas Eaton (Operations Supervisor) 
 
  
IV. PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE 
City Council President Munro led all present in the Pledge of Allegiance. 
 
  
V. APPROVAL OF MINUTES 
No minutes were presented for approval. 
 
  
VI. MAYOR'S MESSAGE  
 
 Appointment of Finance Director 
 Mayor Morse read his message into the record. A summary is included below: 
• Mayor David Morse is pleased to announce the appointment of Bruno Inacio as Finance 
Director. Bruno brings 20 years of experience. Most recently, he served at the Maine Secretary
of State office.  Gave thanks to Laura King for her work and support  during this interim period. 
Thank you to Councilor Chau for serving on the interview panel. 
• The Maine Eviction Prevention program reopened for applications. It provides rental assistance 
for eligible households facing eviction. Payments go directly to participating landlords. 
MaineHousing is accepting applications, and help on the application can be found through 
Project Home & Westbrook General Assistance.  
• Tonight we will see the Collective Bargaining Agreement with the General Unit. Mayor Morse 
provided an overview of how these agreements factor into the municipal and school budgets.  
• Westbrook has been hearing about the Amazon facility in Gorham. Mayor Morse is concerned 
about the traffic impact, and we are paying attention. Westbrook is participating in the MDOT 
traffic study, and press for meaningful measures to address any impacts.  
 
 
  
VII. CITY COUNCIL MESSAGES 
City Council President Munro opened the floor for City Council messages. Councilors provided the following 
updates: 
• President Munro thanked all that came out to the disc golf tournament.  
• Councilor Rairdon wanted to remind folks to please use the microphones so that viewers at home can 
hear. 
 
  
VIII. STUDENT REPRESENTATIVE UPDATE 
There was no Student Representative update. 
 
  
IX. PUBLIC COMMENT 
City Council President Munro opened the floor for the first public comment portion of this meeting. The 
following individuals spoke: No one spoke.  
 
  
X. UNFINISHED BUSINESS 
There was no unfinished business for consideration.  
 
  
XI. ORDERS OF THE DAY (SECOND AND FINAL READING)  
 
 Order 2026-96. Authorizing Acceptance of Federal Asset Forfeiture Funds  
Order 2026-97. Confirming Emergency Expenditure for Replacement Police Vehicle 
Order 2026-98. Authorizing Acceptance & Expenditure of a Edward Byrne Memorial Justice Assistance 
Grant 
Order 2026-99. Authorizing Agreement for Police Department Camera Replacement Project 
Order 2026-100. Authorizing Expenditure for Pershing Way Pump Station Roof Replacement 
Order 2026-101. Authorizing Purchase of Vibratory Plate Compactor for Public Services 
 Motion to approve second and final reading of Orders 2026-96 through 2026-101 
Moved by Councilor Chau, seconded by Councilor Rairdon 
City Council President Munro asked if any Councilor would like to consider any item separately. 
Councilor Chau would like item 2026-102 taken separately.
City Council President Munro opened the floor for comments on the motion. The following individuals 
spoke: No one spoke. 
Motion carried. Order 2026-96 through 2026-101 adopted. (Vote 5-0-2) 
Ayes: McCambridge, Chau, Faulkingham, Rairdon, Munro 
Nays: None 
Absent: Shaughnessy, Turcotte 
 
 Order 2026-102. Approving the 2026 - 2029 Collective Bargaining Agreement with the Westbrook 
General Unit  
 Motion to approve second and final reading of Order 2026-102 
Moved by Councilor Chau, seconded by Councilor Faulkingham 
City Council President Munro asked if any Councilor would like to consider any item separately. No one 
spoke 
City Council President Munro opened the floor for comments on the motion. The following individuals 
spoke: No one spoke 
City Council President Munro opened the floor for comments from the public. The following individuals 
spoke: Marc Fournier (read into the record via email), Angela Holmes (City Administrator) 
Motion carried. Order 2026-102 adopted. (Vote 5-0-2) 
Ayes: McCambridge, Chau, Faulkingham, Rairdon, Munro 
Nays: None 
Absent: Shaughnessy, Turcotte 
 
  
XII. NEW BUSINESS  
 
  
 Orders (One Reading Required)  
 
 Order 2026-103. Authorizing Street Closures for Southern Spring Street and Thomas Drive for Utility 
Installation  
 Motion to approve the first and final reading of the legislation.  
Moved by Councilor Faulkingham, seconded Councilor Rairdon 
City Council President Munro opened the floor for comments on the motion. The following individuals 
spoke: Angela Holmes (City Administrator), Councilor Rairdon, Jennie Franceschi (Assistant City 
Administrator), Contractors for 984 Spring Street, Councilor Chau,  
Motion carried. Order 2026-103 adopted. (Vote 5-0-2) 
Ayes: McCambridge, Chau, Faulkingham, Rairdon, Munro 
Nays: None 
Absent: Shaughnessy, Turcotte 
  
 
 Order 2026-104. Amending the Westbrook Code of Ordinances Regarding the Board of Assessment 
Review, Board of Trustees of the Woodlawn Cemetery, Fair Hearing Authority, Library Advisory 
Committee, Planning Board, Zoning Board of Appeals, and Village Review Overlay Zone Committee  
 Motion to approve the first and final reading of the legislation.  
Moved by Councilor Faulkingham, seconded by Councilor Chau 
City Council President Munro opened the floor for comments on the motion. The following individuals 
spoke: Angela Holmes (City Administrator), Councilor Chau,  
Motion carried. Order 2026-104 adopted. (Vote 5-0-2) 
Ayes: McCambridge, Chau, Faulkingham, Rairdon, Munro
Nays: None 
Absent: Shaughnessy, Turcotte 
  
 
 Order 2026-105. Amending the City Council Rules of Order Relating to Disclosure of Address During 
Public Comment  
 Motion to approve the first and final reading of the legislation.  
Moved by Councilor McCambridge, seconded by Councilor Rairdon 
City Council President Munro opened the floor for comments on the motion. The following individuals 
spoke: Angela Holmes (City Administrator), Councilor Chau, Vice President Shaughnessy, Councilor 
McCambridge, Councilor Rairdon 
Motion carried. Order 2026-105 adopted. (Vote 4-2-1) 
Ayes: Shaughnessy, Faulkingham, Rairdon, Munro 
Nays: McCambridge, Chau 
Absent: Turcotte 
 
  
 Orders (Two Readings Required)  
 
 Order 2026-106. Authorizing Purchase of Portable Traffic Signals for Public Services  
 Motion to approve the first of two readings of the legislation. 
Moved by Vice President Shaughnessy, seconded by Councilor Chau 
City Council President Munro opened the floor for comments on the motion. The following individuals 
spoke: Angela Holmes (City Administrator), Councilor McCambridge, Doug Eaton (Operations 
Supervisor), Mayor Morse, Councilor Rairdon, President Munro 
Motion carried by a show of hands. None opposed. 
 
  
XIII. PUBLIC COMMENT 
City Council President Munro opened the floor for the second and final public comment portion of this meeting. 
The following individuals spoke: No one spoke 
 
  
XIV. REFERRALS 
There were no referrals for consideration.  
 
  
XV. COMMITTEE REPORTS  
 
 The following items remain in their City Council Committees for deliberation. No updates were provided 
by Committee Chairs. 
 
Committee of the Whole 
Board, Commission, Committee Ordinance  
Code of Conduct & Job Descriptions for Elected Officials 
Private Ways Ordinance  
 
Facilities & Streets Committee 
Establishment of Memorial Area 
Policy on Establishing Memorial Areas
Friends of Warren Recreational Area Introductions & Updates 
Haskell Street Traffic Calming 
 
Housing & Economic Development Committee 
Cannabis Dispensary Zoning Regulations  
  
XVI. EXECUTIVE SESSION  
 
 Request to enter into executive session pursuant to 1 M.R.S.A §405-6(A), for discussion regarding an 
appointment of the body or agency and §405-6(E) regarding consultations between a body or agency 
and its attorney concerning the legal rights and duties of the body or agency, inviting the following to 
attend: Mayor, City Administrator, Assistant City Administrator, City Clerk, Legal Counsel, Director of 
Planning & Code Enforcement, Project Manager 
 Motion to enter into Executive Session at 6:56pm as stated above. 
Moved by Councilor Rairdon, second by Council Faulkingham.  
Motion carried by a show of hands. None opposed.  
 
  
XVII. ADJOURNMENT 
The City Council Meeting adjourned directly out of executive session at 8:26pm 
Moved by Councilor Rairdon, seconded by Council Chau. 
Motion carried by a show of hands. None opposed.
